title: Amasis II
summary: King of Egypt after Apries; died before Cambyses invaded (Herodotus 2.172–182, 3.1–10).
description: Added from the Herodotus import (The Histories, tr. Rawlinson). Herodotus gives reign lengths and synchronisms, not BC years, and no tier 1–4 chronology dates this person, so there is no sort year.

sorting_basis.note: No tier gives a birth year (Herodotus is display-only and gives none).

reign.date: “Rhodopis also lived during the reign of Amasis, not of Mycerinus”
reign.citation: Herodotus, Histories 2.134 (tr. George Rawlinson; Roman Roads Media etext, 2013), p. 153 (PDF p. 155)
reign.note: Synchronism: Rhodopis and her fellow slave Aesop belong to the reign of Amasis, "very many years later" than the pyramid builders.

reign.date: “After Apries had been put to death in the way that I have described above, Amasis reigned over Egypt.”
reign.citation: Herodotus, Histories 2.172 (tr. George Rawlinson; Roman Roads Media etext, 2013), p. 170 (PDF p. 172)

reign.date: “Solon the Athenian borrowed this law from the Egyptians”
reign.citation: Herodotus, Histories 2.177 (tr. George Rawlinson; Roman Roads Media etext, 2013), p. 173 (PDF p. 175)
reign.note: Synchronism: Solon adopts a law of Amasis.

reign.date: “he had died after ruling Egypt forty and four years”
reign.citation: Herodotus, Histories 3.10 (tr. George Rawlinson; Roman Roads Media etext, 2013), p. 178 (PDF p. 180)
reign.note: Amasis died before Cambyses arrived; Psammenitus his son was king. DERIVED (not Herodotus's figure): 525 BC (CFAH AP-8) + ½ year (Psammenitus) + 44 = about 570/569 BC for Amasis's accession.
